habitats: The single dyke-dammed spring basin in the low eastern valley
summary: Exactly one landmark tree stands 28–32 m above the low eastern valley's dyke-dammed spring. Its 2–3 m diameter trunk, broad buttresses and flexible crown help resist wind and overturning without guaranteeing storm survival. This self-compatible individual can set fruit without another local adult; its species also has mainland populations. Groundwater supports a conditional dry-season crop for rondo, low peripheral foliage feeds coloso and sheltered crown forks hold alula nests (F18, F19, F21, F26, F27).

links: The rock-spire dyke dams groundwater and sustains the spring.
Reliable water supports a large crown through eastern seasonal drought.
A 2–3 m diameter trunk and spreading structural roots carry its weight.
Buttresses and flexible branches distribute dense-air wind loads.
chains.play: Navigate to the unique crown, locate the spring and climb established root-and-branch routes.
chains.weakness: Water cannot prevent uprooting in failing soil; damaged roots and dead branches create dangerous routes.
observe: Water emerges beside the dyke between spreading roots.
Broad buttresses rise along the massive trunk.
Fine branches flex above a comparatively steady base.

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: Keep exactly one landmark individual, 28–32 m tall with 2–3 m diameter at breast height and substantial buttresses. Place it only at the low eastern spring basin; oxygen does not explain its height. Strict review (2026-11-19): Residual: F21 explicitly places the giant tree at the dyke-dammed spring, and a 28–32 m tree with a 2–3 m trunk is not mechanically extraordinary at F2's 1.05 g. F19's '1.6× Earth's' wind force makes crown reconfiguration and anchorage relevant. Residual weakness: trunk diameter and buttresses alone cannot demonstrate storm stability without crown area, wood properties, root spread and soil strength; flexible branches can also concentrate damaging oscillations.

analogues.mechanism: Buttress-root anchorage supports resistance to overturning; the groundwater subsidy follows F21.

chains.trait: Self-compatible dry-season fruit at a permanent spring
links: Eastern meadow grasses cure during summer.
Groundwater and stored resources permit dry-season fruit development when reproductive conditions are suitable.
Self-compatibility allows the single local landmark adult to set seeded fruit without a second adult, although compatible pollen must still reach receptive flowers.
Rondo eats ripe pulp and transports some intact fruit; discarded viable seeds and unrecovered caches can move seeds beyond the crown.
Seed transport does not demonstrate recruitment, and successful seedlings are not additional landmark giants.
chains.play: Collect ripe fallen fruit and read tracks before entering the shaded feeding hub; distinguish carried seeds from established seedlings.
chains.weakness: Water and self-compatibility do not guarantee pollination or a crop; predictable fruit attracts predators, and most transported seeds may fail to establish.
observe: Soft scented fruit falls beside straw-coloured meadow.
Rondo carries intact fruit and leaves some viable seeds with discarded pulp or in unrecovered caches.
Transported seeds occur beyond the crown without demonstrating a new mature tree.

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: Groundwater permits rather than guarantees fruiting. Dispersed seeds do not authorize duplicate landmark instances. Strict review (2026-11-19): revised: Replaced the irrelevant fruit citation, supplied self-compatible reproduction and specified viable seed transport without equating it with recruitment or duplicate landmarks. Residual: F18 supplies summer drying, F21 the groundwater subsidy and F26 edible fruit; rondo's stated fruit diet and caches support handling and possible seed transport. Self-compatibility removes the need for another genotype but does not ensure pollen transfer, successful fertilization or freedom from inbreeding effects. The chain explicitly retains pollination and resource conditions and separates dispersal from recruitment. Dry-season fruiting is therefore an allowed species strategy, not a necessary consequence of the spring.

analogues.mechanism: Self-compatible reproduction permits a lone adult to produce seeded fruit, while pulp handling and unrecovered caches can transport viable seeds; establishment remains a separate filter.

gameplay.notes: Exactly one mature spring landmark is generated. Coloso can browse only foliage intersecting its actual neck-and-mouth reach from stable ground; the 28–32 m crown is not wholly accessible. Alula uses protected forks for shelter. Climbing requires reachable holds or mature attached vines; branch failure and falls remain consequential at 1.05 g.

placement.slope: Only the designated low eastern spring-basin landmark beside the groundwater-damming dyke; snap altitude directly to the authored spring terrain point.
placement.wetness: Reliable groundwater with aerated roots above permanent saturation.
placement.soil: Deep stable mineral soil and humus adjoining the dyke.
placement.fog: Valley fog is supplementary; groundwater supplies the tree.
placement.density: Exactly one mature landmark instance at the authored spring point inside mapped land. This instance rule does not make the species a singleton: mainland populations exist, and transported seeds or small recruits never instantiate another landmark giant.

generator.seasonal: Evergreen and self-compatible, with a concentrated dry-season fruit crop conditional on pollen transfer, resources and reproductive success.
generator.wind_response: Fine branches yield under gusts while the massive buttressed base resists overturning; extreme storms can break limbs.
